newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia/U.S. bond spread ends under 100 pts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia/U.S. bond spread ends under 100 pts.

text.p: Australian bonds spreads to U.S. 10-year bonds ended at their lowest levels in 2-1/2 years, and traders said that with a bullish market expecting a November rate cut, spreads were likely to remain narrow in the near term.

The spread closed at 99 points but in early trading when there was some talk the Reserve bank of Australia would announce a 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) rate cut, the spread narrowed to 97 points, a level one trader described as "just craziness".
But despite that view, he conceded the spread was likely to remain well bid over the next month given the high level of expectations among investors that interest rates will be cut.
"It's crazy we're here, but while there is still rate cut speculation which is going to last until after the November (RBA) board meeting, you probably can't be a seller of our market," he said.

"They are just holding our market, and if the other markets are performing well, we perform well; if other markets are performing badly, we don't go anywhere ... we just keep crunching on the spreads," he said.
New Zealanders go to the polls this weekend, and pre-election polls point to a Labour-led coaltion government.
The possible loss of power by the ruling National Party has been a negative for NZ bonds, and local bonds have improved their premium to NZ stock this week.
However, traders said as there was some confusion as to the outcome, there were some interested buyers chasing the high NZ yields, and so it was unclear how th emarket will react on Monday.
"There has been a bit of switch activty, but it really is two way interest so, its a bit hard to say what the fallout from New Zealand is going to be at this stage," one trader said.
